surfaces.reason: The canonical entry commits integer outputs, owner credits, fees, burn, distribution and u128 carryover atomically; awards are fresh synthetic outputs and source records remain unchanged. It uses the explicit node 800-permille fee split and default draw policy.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Every node/model/simulator field or observed-state mismatch fails lottery_sim. This record provides no exemption; constructor and bookkeeping checks are simulator representation constraints, not a consensus-admission proof.

surfaces.reason: ActivityBased multiplies value/factor by activity; FeeProportional uses recorded fees and a floating factor discount; PureValueWeighted uses value/factor; UniformPerUtxo counts outputs. Factor, activity and ticket calculations use floats.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: These historical ticket models are research alternatives. They do not select the integer canonical production draw or establish its economics.

surfaces.reason: Pooled accumulates fees until the configured drawing_interval. Immediate distributes per transaction to winners_per_tx; that parameter is a research setting rather than the node block transition cadence.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Neither legacy cadence is production block accounting. Production is tested separately on every supplied block and persistent carryover.

surfaces.reason: This is the legacy lottery module SelectionMode, distinct from the canonical draw enum. Rules use value, sqrt/log weights, max_per_owner, Hybrid alpha, max_age_blocks/age_bonus, cluster factor or entropy_bonus. ValueWeightedWithFloor uses ticket_threshold, decay_rate_per_day, min_eligibility and blocks_per_day. Activity history, tag entropy and simulator owner knowledge are assumed available; selectors can repeat winners.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Owner caps, activity/entropy weighting and these parameterized research policies are not implemented canonical production rules, privacy guarantees or Sybil-resistance results.

surfaces.reason: Legacy floating tickets/factors/activity/entropy and structure_factor split penalties/consolidation discounts affect fees and weights. run_drawing allocates proportional float shares, truncates each payout, clears the pool and records the whole pool. distribute_to_winners uses integer division without production last-winner remainder allocation, in-place credits and activity refresh.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: These paths do not provide production fresh-output accounting, residue conservation or carryover behavior; a legacy modeling difference cannot waive an actual production state failure.

surfaces.reason: LotteryConfig uses base_fee, floating pool_fraction, factor, output_fee_exponent and optional structure/demurrage settings. Its time convention is 4320 blocks/day (20 seconds) and blocks_per_year=4320*365; combined_mechanism comments use 1000 simulation units/BTH. with_consensus_fee instead takes caller-supplied pico_per_unit and preserves the configured blocks_per_year; units are not implicitly node picocredits.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Legacy fee/time/unit approximations must be stated when interpreting results. Selecting shared fee arithmetic does not convert the lottery selection or application into production behavior.

surfaces.reason: The sweep calculates expected-value population redistribution and weights for each Rule. SEED=0xB07A_0902 is documentary; this is not a seeded lottery draw campaign. It uses shared MAINNET_BLOCKS_PER_YEAR, LOTTERY_BASE_FEE_PICO and PICO_PER_BTH with analytic annual demurrage/population assumptions.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Matching constants or expected-value outcomes is not stateful production parity or a profitability proof. This CLI does not call apply_production_block.

surfaces.reason: Stationary capture/window formulas and expected-value honest redistribution compare Burn, UniformAll and WindowedCirculated. SEED=0xB07A_0902_2 is documentary, with no random draws. Fee floors, annual time and BTH/pico conversion use the shared mainnet constants within analytic population assumptions.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: These policy comparisons do not execute the production transition and cannot validate its full state or invalidate the faithful profitability refutation.

surfaces.reason: This expected-value rate-based cap study uses annual/lump accounting, burn/carry policies and shared mainnet year, base-fee and pico-unit constants. SEED=0xB07A_0902_3 is documentary; no random production draws are sampled.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: The modeled rate cap and aggregate economics are not the implemented window-count/block-reward cap or block-by-block payout/carryover equivalence.

surfaces.reason: CurrentCode is expected-value analysis with mirrored kernels/parity goldens: window rho truncated at 10000, payout bounded by block reward, size-based fee floor, eligible free tickets and backlog/epoch assumptions. Other Rules are candidate remedies (per-block/window-length cap, output base fees, no-free eligibility or 1 BTH minimum), not implemented production rules. Capacity compares proposer-slot and block-size bounds. Separate SplitMix64 window_mc uses SEED=0x1682_FA17_0902 and 400 offsets per current setting to sample candidate windows, not production payout draws.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: The faithful flag selects this analysis, not apply_production_block. Mirror parity and candidate-window Monte Carlo do not prove economic safety; the #1682/#1761 profitability refutation and its assumptions remain in force.

surfaces.reason: The shared fee adapter offers ConsensusOnly (consensus floor) and ConsensusPlusRelayMin (max with relay minimum), labeled consensus and consensus+relay. It converts caller units with pico_per_unit, saturates ledger-width amounts and carries sub-unit fee remainder. The production lottery leg receives total_fees already collected; upstream fee-floor resolution and fee mode are external inputs.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Testing the canonical 800-permille split/accounting does not test fee collection, transaction validity or the choice of relay policy. Existing sim_code_parity and faithful parity goldens guard shared constants; they do not establish economics.

surfaces.reason: The caller supplies an ordered candidate snapshot and chooses discovery/window/order and spent-record policy. Later award references resolve from independent node/reference inventory, not simulator outputs. Lean receives these snapshots, including node-derived prior awards, rather than discovering ledger candidates.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: The leg compares arithmetic and application for supplied snapshots; it does not prove candidate discovery, accepted-chain reachability or equivalence of the simulator inventory to an admitted ledger.

surfaces.reason: Initial output identity/value/factor/height and owner mapping are externally registered. The independent reference keeps immutable originals and predicts fresh payouts/owner credits from node results. Public simulator inventory, owner/UTXO totals and metrics are then observed after each step.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: These are Rust state-application checks, not Lean ownership, privacy, cryptographic-outpoint or accepted-chain proofs.

surfaces.reason: Each block supplies emission_share and block_reward already resolved by its caller; the leg exercises their arithmetic use, including saturation and caps, without deriving a monetary schedule.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Lottery correspondence does not validate emission scheduling, principal bounds, monetary policy or economic incentives.

surfaces.reason: Each block supplies an exact 32-byte V2 seed. The lottery_sim composition starts after seed derivation and takes candidate order as supplied.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: This leg does not test V2 hash derivation or RandomX. Wider DRT has a Lean SHA-256 implementation with startup FIPS vectors and supplies RandomX outputs from Rust where applicable; those trust boundaries remain separate.

surfaces.reason: The valid domain has 1-4 strictly increasing blocks, at most 10000 initial/snapshot entries, decimal-string u64 fields/u128 carryover and exact-width hex IDs/seeds. Synthetic output IDs and checked allocator, owner and metric representation impose simulator constraints. Invalid identity/mapping/overflow inputs are exercised separately by atomic-rejection tests.
surfaces.effect_on_production_claims: Constructive finite DRT covers representable valid inputs; these guards are not consensus rules or full-domain proofs. Synthetic IDs and Rust bookkeeping are not modeled cryptographic output identities.
